A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BayesVLM/ProbCosine work. Main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original zero-shot classification, active-learning, corruption, approximation-quality, and computational-cost experiments in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix F, including classification tables and active-learning plots.

M1.justification: The last-layer Laplace/KFAC approximation, ProbCosine moments, probit predictions, targeted acquisition, and online updates are retained. v3 explains directional likelihoods and surrogate models more explicitly, but the factors, Jacobians, and algorithms already documented in v2 do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the seven zero-shot benchmarks, OfficeHome and ImageNet cross-domain tasks, EuroSAT example, and LAION/ImageNet estimation and calibration data. Newly named checkpoint-training corpora in v3 Appendix E.1 document existing models rather than establish added coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain vanilla CLIP/SigLIP, temperature scaling, TTA, mean predictions for ProLIP/PCME++, and random/entropy acquisition variants. Moving ProLIP and PCME++ tables does not change comparator membership. Newly discussed related methods are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 corrects the main-text pseudo-data-count selection rule to minimizing NLPD; v2 Section 4.2 says highest NLPD. Since v2 Appendix E.2 already specifies minimization, this corrects the reported protocol rather than establishing reruns. The proxy subset, search grids, and training settings otherwise match.

E4.justification: The corruption example, Gaussian-versus-KDE approximation check, Wasserstein-versus-cosine ablation, Hessian sample-count analysis, hyperparameter plots, and runtime analysis all have counterparts in v2. Reorganization adds no new analytical experiment.

E5.justification: Both retain test-set standard errors, paired t-tests at p = 0.05, Hessian error bands over 10 random subsets, and timing averages over 1000 runs. No changed uncertainty-estimation practice or repeated-run count is documented.

E6.justification: Matched numerical tables and plotted results are retained, but the reported comparative finding is corrected. v2 Table 2 claims consistent superiority across ACC, NLPD, and ECE; v3 Table 1 describes comparable ACC/NLPD and better ECE. Flowers-102 accuracy remains 68.87 for BayesVLM versus 68.99 for CLIP, illustrating corrected reporting rather than a performance gain.

T1.justification: Most derivations remain, with more explicit likelihood assumptions in v3. However, the covariance rewrite introduces a non-equivalent inconsistency: v2 Eq. (17) correctly uses inverse Hessian H^-1, whereas v3 Eq. (15) defines Sigma as the inverse Hessian and Eq. (16) then uses Sigma^-1 as covariance.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain. The conclusion is narrowed: v2 explicitly claims consistent NLPD/ECE improvements over CLIP and SigLIP, while v3 replaces that assertion with a general claim of efficient, well-calibrated uncertainty estimates.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix F.6 adds a hypothesis linking TTA's CIFAR accuracy losses to cropping small images and explains some TTA gains through augmentation averaging. It removes v2's specific large-tau/MAP explanation of SigLIP's data mismatch. The stated training-data, Gaussian-embedding, and last-layer limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix E.1 documents implementation sources, licenses, PCME++ and ProLIP ViT-B/16 checkpoints, PCME++ training corpora, and ProLIP access information. These are additional disclosures for retained experiments; hardware, fine-tuning hyperparameters, and the paper's code-access statement remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning around Bayesian adapters, prompt distributions, ensembles, training-free OOD detection, and Bayesian test-time adaptation, including BayesAdapter and CLIPScope. Active-learning coverage expands to diversity, parametric acquisition, and LLM fine-tuning approaches. Several generic uncertainty references are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, posterior-construction explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. v3 reorganizes experimental setup into named paragraphs, shortens main-text acquisition details, relocates algorithms to the appendix, and adds appendix roadmaps. This exceeds routine copyediting.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. The EuroSAT figure is rearranged and moved into the introduction; ProLIP and PCME++ tables exchange main-text/appendix placement; computational costs move into the main text; and the desiderata table is removed. Plot sizing, ticks, captions, and algorithm placement also change.

improvement.justification: v3 provides clearer posterior-construction explanations, checkpoint provenance, and a more accurate main zero-shot comparison. These benefits are countered by newly inconsistent covariance/precision expressions in Appendix B.2, Eqs. (15)–(16), and Appendix C.1, Eq. (49). The gains in documentation and reporting coexist with reduced mathematical consistency in central calculations, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
